publication_date_basis: GitHub commit time of the author's commit 56c59854 in Majdoddin/formal-math (the repository push was 2026-11-20T17:58:14Z). Version 2 of arXiv:2610.17420; it is not yet on arXiv. The author reported it in bigospeedrun/site issue 25.
theorem: Corollary 24.1(e) (also stated as Corollary D in Section 1.3 of version 2), via Theorem C and Corollary 9.4
model_check: Corollary 24.1(e): Exact Triangle (also in its all-edges version), the (min,+)-product and APSP on directed n-vertex graphs with integer weights of absolute value at most n^nu and no negative cycles are solved deterministically in time n^(3-0.00612+o(1)) = n^(2.99388+o(1)), on a word RAM with O(log n)-bit words. The author says Theorem C gives O(n^(3-epsilon*gamma+epsilon/(2r)) (log n)^(r+5)) for every fixed r, here with H(2/25, 0.0765) from Corollary 9.4, so every exponent above 2.99388 is proved, not 2.99388 itself. The fixed-width program and word-width quantifiers of EndStatement are an algorithmic interpretation, not a checked formal statement equivalence. Source comparison, not a proof check.

lean.scope: Running times are not formalised (the author says so in issue 25). The Lean folders check the identities, counts and reductions of version 1, not running times.

verification: Written proof, not peer reviewed. The numerical certificates behind H(2/25, 0.0765) are exact-rational scripts in the repository (scripts/ at that commit). The running time is not formalised in Lean. No Big O Speedrun proof check. Evidence remains Claimed.
